name: Isolated Diffuse Palmoplantar Keratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Diffuse Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Diffuse hyperkeratosis involving the entire palmar and plantar surfaces
No associated nail dystrophy or abnormalities
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance or sporadic occurrence
Exclusion of syndromic or systemic causes of palmoplantar keratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of diffuse hyperkeratosis on palms and soles with exclusion of other syndromic keratodermas and absence of nail involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist in diagnosis but is not mandatory.

laboratory: Histopathology showing marked hyperkeratosis with preserved granular layer
Negative fungal cultures to exclude tinea infections
genetic: Mutations in keratin genes (e.g., KRT9) reported in some familial cases
other: Clinical examination revealing symmetrical diffuse palmoplantar hyperkeratosis without systemic involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Localized hyperkeratosis primarily on pressure points
Presence of nail dystrophy or other ectodermal abnormalities
Systemic features such as hearing loss or cardiac involvement
Genetic mutations in syndromic keratoderma genes

redFlags: Rapid progression of hyperkeratosis with systemic symptoms
Presence of nail dystrophy or other ectodermal abnormalities
Signs of secondary infection with systemic toxicity
